summary: Ciubotaru–Harris v1 asserts generic Ramanujan propagation (Theorem5.4), conditional complementary-series propagation (Theorem1.11) and exclusion of extraneous points with a discrete-series anchor (Theorem10.3). The extraction records their hypotheses and existing proof gaps, not unconditional repaired proofs. Its local classification imports the existing representation foundations and nilpotent-weight theory. This fix restricts the source-derived extraneous lists to real/central-compact parameters: E11’s fully geometric G2 zero-orbit witness also invalidates the unrestricted exceptional endpoint of Theorem8.5/Remark8.7 (linked E18). General compact-part classification and global uses are explicitly gated, separately from the existing stratum-recognition gap. Theorem4.2 is moved to an early arithmetic prefix with FA.6/GS/SR/DWP inputs and a source-gated, pending GHS globalization/purity obligation; ownership does not solve E10. There are 83 items (2 library, 11 planned, 70 missing), four routes with sizes 11, 29, 27, 3, thirteen prerequisites and eighteen source findings. Historical table/orbit certificates and previous reviews are retained without a fresh exhaustive re-audit.

items.name: Nonzero sl2 triple
items.statement: Over a commutative ring R and an R-Lie algebra L, a triple (h,e,f) satisfies h != 0, [e,f]=h, [h,e]=2e, [h,f]=-2f.
items.note: Pinned Sl2.lean lines 35-49 read. The paper also requires the zero orbit; this library item does not cover it.

items.name: Zero-orbit comparison
items.statement: In characteristic zero, extend the nonzero-triple interface by the zero triple and prove that h=0 forces e=f=0; its filtration is concentrated in weight zero.

items.name: Jacobson-Morozov existence
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, every nilpotent e occurs in a triple satisfying the sl2 relations, allowing the zero triple.

items.name: Triples and nilpotent orbits
items.statement: In the same setting, taking the raising element induces a bijection between adjoint-conjugacy classes of triples and nilpotent orbits.

items.name: Tensor-compatible triple filtration
items.statement: For each finite-dimensional representation V, use the integral h-eigenspace decomposition to define Fil_i(V) as the sum of eigenspaces of weights at most i. Construct the functor on intertwiners and its tensor, dual and underlying-vector-space comparisons.
items.note: The appendix tables list the graded dimensions dim gr_i, not the cumulative dim Fil_i (sourceIssues E4); cumulative sums recover the filtration.

items.name: Recognition from every representation
items.statement: Let g∨ be a semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. If two sl2-triples satisfy dim Fil_i(V) = dim Fil'_i(V) for every finite-dimensional representation V of g∨ and every integer i, they are conjugate under the adjoint action of G∨.
items.note: All representations, not just the standard or adjoint representation. Very-even orthogonal orbits require a half-spin separator. Certified 29 Sep 2026 for the exceptional types by a Bala–Carter enumeration (item exceptional-adjoint-separation): the adjoint graded dimensions alone separate all nilpotent orbits of G2, F4, E6, E7 and E8. The appendix's inference from E8 to its Levi subalgebras is not valid as stated (sourceIssues E6), but the conclusion holds.

items.name: Integral spectrum of a triple
items.statement: For an sl2-triple (h, e, f) in a Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero and a finite-dimensional module M, every eigenvalue of h on M is an integer; over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, M is the direct sum of the h-eigenspaces at the integers, so h acts diagonalizably. (The zero triple is item zero-triple-adapter.)
items.note: Built in Tau Ceti at f790474 (TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Sl2/Spectrum.lean:147, 305), the 'diagonalizability and the integer spectrum' bullet of LieHighestWeight Layer 0, which the extraction had cited as a plan.

items.name: Integer Weil weights
items.statement: For q>1 and a nonzero algebraic number a, weight w in Z means that every complex embedding has absolute value q^(w/2). Algebraic integrality is a separate predicate.

items.name: Geometric local parameter
items.statement: For F=k((t)), ell != char(k), a semisimple ell-adic L-parameter is geometric when Frobenius eigenvalues in a faithful algebraic realization are algebraic Weil q-numbers of integer weights; prove independence of faithful realization and Frobenius lift under the source hypotheses.

items.name: Pure Weil-Deligne representation
items.statement: With Frob_u a geometric Frobenius (so ϕ(Frob_u)Nϕ(Frob_u)^{−1} = q^{−1}N and N lowers Frobenius weights by 2), let W_aV be the sum of the generalized eigenspaces of ϕ(Frob_u) of weight ≤ a, a (ϕ, N)-stable filtration. A Weil–Deligne representation (ϕ, N) is pure of weight w if all Frobenius weights are integers and N^i : gr_{w+i}V → gr_{w−i}V is an isomorphism for every i ≥ 0.
items.note: Import the local monodromy and purity interface of DWP.5. A comparison of arithmetic/geometric Frobenius and the sign convention for N remains an application-specific obligation, not a duplicate carrier. Definition 2.6 prints (iii) as N^i : gr_{w−i} → gr_{w+i}, which is inconsistent with (ii) (sourceIssues E9); this is the intended monodromy-weight purity.

items.name: Functorial mixed weight filtration
items.statement: For a lisse mixed rational ell-adic sheaf with integral weights, construct the unique functorial strict weight filtration with pure graded pieces. Purity does not assert arithmetic semisimplicity.

items.name: One geometric boundary place
items.statement: Let U be an open of a smooth proper curve over a finite field and L a lisse ell-adic local system. Under Proposition 2.7's geometric local representation hypothesis at u outside U, all unramified fibers have integral Weil weights.

items.name: Purity of the boundary graded pieces
items.statement: Under the preceding curve and geometricity hypotheses, the local Weil-Deligne representation at u of each weight-i graded piece is pure of weight i.
items.note: Apply DWP.5 to the pure graded pieces supplied by DWP.8; this is curve weight-monodromy, not a mixed-characteristic conjecture.

items.name: Finite-level cuspidal finiteness
items.statement: For semisimple G over the global function field and compact level U, the E-valued cuspidal automorphic forms form a finite E-module, and every function in A0(G, U, E) is supported on a finite subset of X_U, independent of E, when E is a noetherian Z[1/p]-algebra embedded in the chosen algebraically closed coefficient field.

items.name: Cuspidal scalar extension
items.statement: With the hypotheses of Proposition 3.1, extension from E to the chosen algebraically closed coefficient field commutes with the space of finite-level cuspidal forms.

items.name: Algebraic cuspidal Hecke eigenvalues
items.statement: The unramified Hecke eigenvalues on the finite-level cuspidal space are algebraic numbers. For E large enough, H_S(G, U) ⊗ E acts semisimply on A0(G, U, E) with finitely many eigenspaces, G(A_K) preserves A0(G, Q), so every cuspidal π has a model over a number field and A0(G, Q̄) = ⊕ m(π)π (§3.1, pp. 8–9). Keep the finite-module and coefficient-model inputs explicit.

items.name: Cuspidal excursion decomposition
items.statement: At fixed level, construct the commutative excursion algebra, its generalized-eigenspace decomposition of cusp forms, and the corresponding continuous semisimple global L-parameters. Do not impose uniqueness from the Hecke eigencharacter alone.

items.name: Unramified Frobenius compatibility
items.statement: For a parameter appearing in the cuspidal excursion decomposition, its unramified Frobenius class equals the local Satake class of the associated Hecke character, with coefficient-embedding and normalization comparisons.

items.name: Semisimple local-global comparison
items.statement: Restriction of a cuspidal global parameter to a local Weil group, followed by semisimplification, depends only on the local representation and agrees with the stated local assignment. This is not full Weil-Deligne compatibility.

items.name: Normalized local induction and Jacquet functors
items.statement: For a reductive group over a nonarchimedean local field, construct normalized parabolic induction and Jacquet functors with the chosen square root of the modulus character and valid coefficient hypotheses.

items.name: Geometric representation
items.statement: A smooth irreducible local representation defined over a number field is geometric when its semisimple local parameter is geometric in Definition 2.5. The coefficient model and embedding comparisons are part of the definition/API.

items.name: Geometric discrete series
items.statement: A discrete-series representation with geometric central character is geometric. For semisimple G the central-character condition is automatic in the source application.
items.note: Requires the actual local-parameter theorem; this is not ordinary smooth representation theory alone. The proof ('point 5 follows from Theorem 4.2') goes through [GHS]'s Weil–Deligne purity of discrete series (item ghs-discrete-series-purity), not through the general step (2) of the §4.1 sketch. Coordinate this input with the explicit early arithmetic-prefix/GHS request, retaining the pending supplier and its source hypotheses. It is not supplied by the final Theorem5.4 application or the unproved general geometricity sketch E10.

items.name: Temperedness after an embedding
items.statement: For a Qbar-model and an embedding iota:Qbar -> C, iota-temperedness means temperedness of scalar extension along iota. Absolute temperedness requires every such embedding.

items.name: Galois conjugation of discrete series
items.statement: For the semisimple local groups in Section 4.1, discrete series admit number-field models and their conjugates remain discrete series. Do not generalize to arbitrary reductive groups with unrestricted transcendental unitary central character.
items.note: Attributed to [GHS] (p. 11: 'the following theorem is proved in [GHS]'); v1 gives only a sketch, 'Complete proofs of the two theorems will appear elsewhere'. Step (1) invokes Beuzart-Plessis's appendix to [GHS] for globalization; the freshly read Appendix Lemma A.1 and Proposition 3.10 supply same cuspidal support, so a precise isolation/support-descent bridge remains required for a number-field model of the prescribed representation. Step (2)'s general geometricity assertion is the gap E10. Move this item to the early arithmetic prefix of GlobalShtukasPartIIRamanujanArthur, before Theorem5.4 and the nongeneric applications. Import FA.6 coefficient models, GS.5/GS.7 cusp parameters and local–global comparison, and SR.2/SR.3 normalized induction, Jacquet exponents and Casselman’s criterion. Use the exact source-gated GHS supplier request below. This ownership repair does not solve E10 or prove Theorem4.3. No whole global consumer is imported back into the local classification.

supplierContract.groupScope: Connected semisimple G over F=k((t)), irreducible complex discrete series; its finite center gives finite-order central character. A reductive-group extension must state an algebraic/geometric central character and its globalization compatibility, not arbitrary transcendental unitary characters.
supplierContract.gate: Actual number-field descent and embedding-stable exponents from independently justified discrete-series purity/globalization. Source-version-specific residue bounds remain explicit; the freshly checked GHSv3 Theorem1.2 assumes p>3. Scope outside that range needs a separate source.
supplierContract.order: GHS gated input plus FA.6/GS/SR/DWP → arithmetic prefix → global applications (Theorem5.4 etc.). The local classification independently feeds those applications; it does not import this whole global PartII.

api.name: DiscreteSeriesArithmetic.numberFieldModel
api.statement: For the stated semisimple scope and independently established source hypotheses, descend the discrete series to a number field; make local-isolation or finite-length cuspidal-support descent explicit.

api.name: DiscreteSeriesArithmetic.embeddingStableExponents
api.statement: Use the independently supplied discrete-series geometricity/purity to make the normalized Jacquet-exponent absolute values independent of complex embedding; apply Casselman with the chosen modulus normalization.

api.name: DiscreteSeriesArithmetic.conjugate_discrete
api.statement: The conjugated number-field model remains discrete series under every embedding, without using Theorem5.4 or the ungated general step(2) of §4.1.

acceptance.name: DiscreteSeriesArithmetic.semisimple_center
acceptance.statement: For semisimple G the finite-center character is of finite order and satisfies the geometric central-character condition; retain all non-central discrete-series inputs.

acceptance.name: DiscreteSeriesArithmetic.transcendental_center
acceptance.statement: For G_m an arbitrary unitary unramified character can have transcendental Frobenius value, so unitary central character alone cannot imply a number-field model.

acceptance.name: DiscreteSeriesArithmetic.no_global_circularity
acceptance.statement: The arithmetic-prefix proof must remain independent of the final Theorem5.4 global temperedness endpoint and of local generic spherical exclusion; reject a proof that uses either to establish its own discrete-series anchor.

items.sourceNoteBeforeArithmeticSupplierRepair: Attributed to [GHS] (p. 11: 'the following theorem is proved in [GHS]'); v1 gives only a sketch, 'Complete proofs of the two theorems will appear elsewhere'. Step (1) of the sketch uses Beuzart-Plessis's appendix to [GHS] (every discrete series is a local component of a cuspidal automorphic representation); step (2) is the gap E10.

items.name: Embedding independence in the cuspidal application
items.statement: For a number-field model of a cuspidal global representation as in Theorem 4.3, a local component that is tempered after one complex embedding is tempered after every complex embedding.
items.note: Only sketched in v1 ('The proof of Theorem 4.3 is similar'), through step (2) of the §4.1 sketch, which is the gap E10. The tempered case of Theorem 5.4 uses it (p. 15).

items.name: Aubert-Zelevinsky semisimple compatibility
items.statement: For the tempered local representations of Proposition 4.5, the Aubert-Zelevinsky involution preserves supercuspidal support and hence the semisimple local parameter. No equality of monodromy operators is asserted.

items.name: Spherical parameter dictionary
items.statement: For unramified G and a hyperspecial K, identify irreducible K-spherical representations with the appropriate relative-Weyl orbits of unramified parameters; retain Frobenius action and q-half normalization.

items.name: Tempered spherical real part
items.statement: Write a spherical Satake parameter as a compact part times q^nu, with dominant real nu. In the source unramified setting the spherical representation is tempered exactly when nu=0.

items.name: Weight classes and constant-field twists
items.statement: For the semisimple local systems tau composed with sigma in Section 5, decompose into constant-field character twists of systems with integral weights, retaining the character equivalence relation and the uniqueness asserted in (5.5).
items.note: Use DWP.8 and GLn purity; do not infer integer weights directly from real iota-weights.

items.name: Lifting the dual-group parameter
items.statement: For G not adjoint, restrict σ to Gal(K^sep/K′) for a finite extension K′ over which it lifts to ^L G^ad (p. 14 and footnote 6), and run the argument over the corresponding cover X′ with the test representation τ0. The paper states this for types C_n and D_n; non-adjoint groups of types A_{n−1} (n even), B_n and E_7 need it too (sourceIssues E12). Construct the cover and track Frobenius powers and residue cardinalities.
items.locator: arXiv:2311.15300v1, Proof of Theorem 5.4, p. 14, and footnote 6
items.note: This is parameter restriction, not an assumed cuspidal automorphic base-change theorem.

items.name: Half-integrality in a representation
items.statement: A real parameter ν is half-integral with respect to a finite-dimensional g∨-representation V when ⟨χ, ν⟩ ∈ ½Z for every weight χ of V; the Satake parameter s = s_c·s_ν is then called geometric with respect to V. This is a condition on the real part, not algebraicity of the compact Satake factor.

items.name: Generic spherical unitary region
items.statement: For split quasi-simple adjoint G and real Satake parameters s_ν: C0 = {ν ∈ t∨_R : ⟨α∨, ν⟩ ≥ 0 for all simple α}; U0^g = {ν ∈ C0 : ⟨α∨, ν⟩ ≠ 1 for all α∨ ∈ Φ∨,+, and L(ν) is unitary}, the spherical generic unitary representations with real Satake parameter; C_{0,h} = {ν ∈ C0 : w0(ν) = −ν} ⊇ U0^g; and A0 = {ν ∈ C0 : ⟨γ∨, ν⟩ < 1} (γ∨ the highest coroot). The unitarity of L(s_c s_ν) with s_c non-central is not governed by U0^g (sourceIssues E11).

items.name: Exclusion at nonzero integral root values
items.statement: If ν ∈ C0 and ⟨α∨, ν⟩ ∈ Z_{>0} for some positive coroot α∨, then ν ∉ U0^g (for real parameters; the proof uses that U0^g is a union of alcoves, Theorem 6.9).

items.name: Type A half-integral candidates
items.statement: For PGL(n), the dominant adjoint-half-integral generic unitary real parameters are {0} if n is odd and {0, omega_(n/2)/2} if n is even, using the paper numbering.

items.name: Type B half-integral candidates
items.statement: For SO(2n+1), the corresponding set is {0,omega_1/2} in the source root numbering.

items.name: Type C half-integral candidates
items.statement: For PSp(2n), the corresponding set is {0,omega_n/2} in the source root numbering.

items.name: Type D half-integral candidates
items.statement: For PSO(2n), the set is {0,omega_1/2,omega_2/2,omega_n/2} when n is even and {0,omega_n/2} when n is odd, under the source rank conventions.

items.name: Type E7 half-integral candidates
items.statement: For adjoint split E7, the dominant adjoint-half-integral generic unitary region consists of 0 and omega_7/2.

items.name: Other exceptional types
items.statement: For each of split adjoint G2, F4, E6 and E8, the dominant adjoint-half-integral generic unitary region contains only zero.
items.note: A complete extraction must split the four independent root calculations further.

items.name: Testing only the highest weight
items.statement: If nu is half-integral for the adjoint representation, it is half-integral for the irreducible representation of highest weight lambda exactly when <lambda,nu> is in (1/2)Z.

items.name: Fundamental representations exclude nonzero candidates
items.statement: In the respective cases of Proposition 6.31 the displayed fundamental representation pairs with the extra candidate by 1/4, or by 3/4 for E7. For D-type both spin and standard tests are needed to eliminate all candidates.
items.note: Source root numbering and global availability of these representations must be checked; no replacement by the adjoint test alone. The test representations τ0 of ^L G restricting to V(λ∨) (Theorem 5.4, table (i)–(v)) exist only after the reduction to adjoint G (E12).

items.name: Local generic temperedness test
items.statement: For split quasi-simple adjoint G and a real Satake parameter s = s_ν (or s_c central): if L(s_ν) is generic and unitary, then ν is half-integral for the adjoint representation and the fundamental representations of Proposition 6.31 only if ν = 0, so L(s) is tempered.
items.note: Corollary 6.32(1) is printed for every s = s_c s_ν, and then it is false: a generic unitary spherical representation of G2 with s_c the involution whose centralizer is of type A1 × Ã1 and ν = ½ω2 is a counterexample (sourceIssues E11). The proof of Theorem 5.4 needs a further argument at places where the compact part is not central.

items.name: Transfer of the real unitary locus
items.statement: For the unramified nonsplit adjoint groups of Section 7 and real nu fixed by the pinned diagram automorphism tau, the spherical quotients for G and the associated split group G(tau) are unitary, respectively generic unitary, simultaneously.

items.name: Nonsplit generic test with an exclusion
items.statement: For an unramified nonsplit quasi-simple adjoint group other than the quasi-split PSU(2n + 1), and a real Satake parameter s = s_ν (or s_c central): if L^G(s_ν) is generic and unitary and ν is half-integral for all finite-dimensional representations of G∨ ⋊ ⟨τ⟩, then ν = 0.
items.note: Corollary 7.5 is printed for s = s_c s_ν, and its proof passes from L^G(s) to L^G(ν) as in Corollary 6.32, so the same restriction applies (sourceIssues E11). The representations of G∨ ⋊ ⟨τ⟩ used are V ⊕ V^τ and the sum of the two half-spin representations.

items.name: Residual odd-unitary candidate
items.statement: For the excluded odd-dimensional quasi-split unitary group, the argument leaves nu=0 and nu=omega_n/2; the spin representation that excludes the latter for the simply connected fixed dual does not descend to the actual fixed dual SO(2n+1). This is not an automorphic counterexample.

items.name: Generic function-field temperedness
items.statement: Let K be a global function field, G connected absolutely simple over K, and pi cuspidal. Assume pi_v is unramified generic, G at v is unramified quasi-split but not the odd-dimensional quasi-split unitary form, and pi_u is tempered at some place u. Then pi_w is tempered at every place w where pi is unramified and G is unramified quasi-split. Use the coefficient interpretation of Section 4.
items.note: This is the author-v1 statement, not a verified transcription of the 2025 accepted revision. The proof applies Corollary 6.32(1) to s_v(σ) with arbitrary compact part, where it fails (E11); it relies on Theorem 4.3, whose sketch has the gap E10; and its reduction to adjoint G is written only for types C and D (E12). The 'more generally' clause should allow any place u (E13).

items.name: Propagation of unramified genericity
items.statement: Under Theorem 5.4, the unramified quasi-split local components in Corollary 5.7 are generic; for globally quasi-split G this holds almost everywhere.

items.name: Kazhdan-Lusztig parameter data
items.statement: For split quasi-simple G, an Iwahori parameter consists of semisimple s, nilpotent e with Ad(s)e=qe, and a Springer-type irreducible representation of the component group of their joint centralizer. Connected-center and general-isogeny classification inputs are distinct.

items.name: Nilpotent partition of the spherical dual
items.statement: Assign to L(s) the nilpotent orbit of the open-orbit raising element in its Aubert-Zelevinsky dual. Define Sph(G,O) and intersect with the unitary dual to obtain CS(G,O). Construct the partition and its normalization at q^(h/2).

items.name: Complementary series from the triple centralizer
items.statement: For G quasi-simple and k-split (the standing hypothesis of §8) and O other than 4A1 in E8: if a unitary spherical parameter has real part h/2 + ν relative to the reductive centralizer of the triple, then ν lies in the zero complementary series of the associated centralizer group. Quoted from [Ba, BC1, Ci1, Ci2].

items.name: Extraneous real parameter
items.statement: For a geometric unitary spherical parameter in CS(G,O), its real part is extraneous when it differs from h/2, the central point attached to O.

items.name: Symplectic-dual extraneous parameters
items.statement: Restrict this classification to s=s_c q^ν with s_c=1 or s_c central in G∨, retaining geometricity in Definition2.5 and the connected-center hypothesis on G. Do not infer the same list for arbitrary noncentral compact parts from the real part alone. For connected-center G with dual Sp(2n), write the nilpotent partition with multiplicities r_i, sum i*r_i=2n and r_i even for odd i. The additional real parameters are h/2+(1/2) sum over even j with r_j>=3 of epsilon_j*omega^j_floor(r_j/2), with epsilon_j in {0,1}, not all zero.
items.note: The proof later prints an odd j where the theorem and centralizer decomposition require even j; resolve against the final version. Resolved: the theorem's even j is right; the proof's 'odd' is a misprint (sourceIssues E2, confirmed by review). The partition/parity data are retained as the real/central-compact interface; their arbitrary-compact completeness is not certified by this repair. A noncentral s_c changes the relevant root centralizer and spherical stratum. The requested centralizer analysis must independently test this family; the G₂ example alone neither disproves nor exhaustively repairs its list.

items.name: Exceptional extraneous-orbit list
items.statement: Restrict this classification to s=s_c q^ν with s_c=1 or s_c central in G∨, retaining geometricity in Definition2.5 and the connected-center hypothesis on G. Do not infer the same list for arbitrary noncentral compact parts from the real part alone. In that restricted sector the source-derived exceptional list has B3 and A1+tilde-A1 in F4, D5(a1)+A1 in E7, and D6,A6,A4+A2,A2+2A1 in E8, with the F4 B3 coordinate corrected by E5 to ω₁+½ω₃+½ω₄. The real/central-compact list has no G2 or E6 entry. This is not a complete list for arbitrary compact factors: the geometric G2 parameter (aα₁+bα₂)(s)=(−1)^a q^(b/2), ν=½ω₂, lies in CS(G2,0) with nonzero real part. General compact-part classification requires the centralizer-of-s_c reduction and a new exhaustive proof; adding this one point does not prove exhaustiveness.
items.note: Exact coweight vectors are recorded in the report. Their computation certificates and separate itemization remain completion work. The F4 B3 coordinate printed as ω₁+ω₂+½ω₃+½ω₄ must be ω₁+½ω₃+½ω₄ (sourceIssues E5, an error confirmed by review against Ciubotaru's F4 classification). The case analysis of Theorem 8.5(4) uses the list of exceptional nilpotent orbits with the types of their reductive centralizers ('see the tables in [Ca]'); it belongs with the nilpotent-orbit Part II. Scope repair of Theorem8.5/Remark8.7: E18 links the already confirmed E11 witness to this additional false endpoint. All weights of dual G2 are integral root combinations, so the witness has Weil eigenvalues of integer weight in every representation, not just a half-integral real part. Ad(s) has no q-eigenvalue; its open nilpotent orbit is0 and central point is1 (real exponent0). Its connected center is trivial. The source proof applies Theorem6.14 to a set of real parts as though they were real unitary parameters; that does not justify arbitrary noncentral s_c.
items.sourceClaimBeforeCompactScopeRepair: Under Theorem 8.5 geometricity and connected-center hypotheses, the exceptional orbits admitting additional real parameters are B3 and A1+tilde-A1 in F4; D5(a1)+A1 in E7; and D6, A6, A4+A2, A2+2A1 in E8. There are none in G2 or E6.

acceptance.name: ExtraneousClassification.g2_geometric_zero_orbit
acceptance.statement: For q>1, (aα₁+bα₂)(s)=(−1)^a q^(b/2) has root values −1,√q,−√q,√q,−√q,−q; no root value is q^±1. Kato’s stabilizer criterion and the irreducible hermitian path give a unitary generic L(s). Every G2 weight gives a Weil eigenvalue of integer weight; Ad(s)_q=0, so s∈CS(G2,0) and Re(s)=½ω₂≠0. Reject the unrestricted no-G2 list.

acceptance.name: ExtraneousClassification.central_compact_scope
acceptance.statement: If s_c is central, the root values and associated nilpotent q-eigenspace agree with the real parameter; require an explicit comparison preserving unitarity/geometricity before applying the restricted list.

acceptance.name: ExtraneousClassification.compact_stratum_required
acceptance.statement: Recognizing ν by all representation-indexed real weights does not recover s_c or the nilpotent stratum. The noncentral G2 witness must not be tested against the real generic region U₀^g merely because ν is half-integral.

items.name: Exceptional 4A1 region exclusion
items.statement: For the extra E8,4A1 unitary region in (8.8), the ordered coordinates cannot all lie in (1/2)Z or all in 1/4+(1/2)Z. Thus the extra region contributes no adjoint-half-integral parameter.
items.note: This is only the finite half-lattice exclusion inside the real E8,4A1 region (8.8). It supplies no unrestricted classification for noncentral s_c and no proof that every arbitrary-compact E8 point reduces to this region. Preserve the finite inequality computation separately from the new compact-part analysis.
items.classificationScope: finite real-region inequality, not arbitrary-compact exhaustiveness

items.name: Explicit discrete-spectrum hypotheses
items.statement: For the nongeneric global theorem require a chosen nonzero parameter summand compatible with the unramified Hecke action and local restrictions. In the cuspidal case use the established excursion construction; outside it retain the finite-level rationality and discrete-spectrum decomposition/Satake hypotheses of Section 9 as assumptions.
items.note: The introduction calls the displayed equation Conjecture 9.3. No conjectural assertion is entered here as a proved theorem. The numbered conjecture is 9.5, not the display (9.3) (sourceIssues E1).

items.name: Conditional rationality of the discrete spectrum
items.statement: Assuming Conjecture 9.1 and the Section 9 coefficient setup, unramified discrete-spectrum Hecke eigenvalues are algebraic and irreducible discrete automorphic representations admit number-field models.
items.note: The two conclusions still need separate items in the completed extraction.

items.name: Representation-indexed weight pattern
items.statement: For a geometric semisimple parameter s, record for every irreducible algebraic representation tau the finitely supported function i |-> multiplicity of weight i among the Frobenius eigenvalues of tau(s).

items.name: Weight patterns determine the real part
items.statement: If two geometric semisimple parameters have identical weight patterns for every algebraic representation, their positive real torus parts are Weyl-conjugate. This does not recover the compact factors.

items.name: Conditional complementary-series propagation
items.statement: In the discrete-spectrum setup of Theorem 1.11, assume an actual compatible global parametrization, a split place v with pi_v in CS(G,N), and a geometric local component at u in S. The source asserts that all split unramified components belong to CS(G,N), with the same central or extraneous real parameter class.
items.note: Review the step from real-part recognition to nilpotent-stratum recognition, as well as the nonadjoint parameter-lifting reduction. This checkpoint does not certify that proof step. Its hypothesis is Conjectures 9.1 and 9.5 (sourceIssues E1). The step from Proposition 10.2 to 'the same complementary series' remains open: the stratum of s depends on its compact part, which Proposition 10.2 does not recover. Additional gate from E18: any use of Theorem8.5/Remark8.7 must either establish the real/central-compact hypothesis at every place of use or import a newly exhaustive arbitrary-compact classification with centralizer-of-s_c and orbit tracking. A geometric parameter with connected center alone is insufficient. Preserve the separate gap from real-part recognition to nilpotent-stratum recognition. The local G2 witness is not asserted to occur in a global cuspidal packet; no global counterexample is claimed.
items.proofState: Unproved target: existing global-parametrization/stratum obligations plus the explicit compact-part classification gate; not solved by this fix.

items.name: Boundary and generic weight array
items.statement: For each representation τ, a(i, k) is the dimension of the weight-k generalized eigenspace of Frob_u in the fibre at the ramified place u of gr_i(L(π, τ)). Row sums are n_v, column sums are n_u, and the purity of the local monodromy filtration gives a(i, i + k) = a(i, i − k) (10.4).

items.name: Lexicographic weight comparison
items.statement: Let a:Z x Z -> N have finite support and satisfy a(i,i+j)=a(i,i-j). Set r_i=sum_j a(i,j) and c_i=sum_j a(j,i). Either a is diagonal and r=c, or at the largest index where r and c differ one has c_i>r_i.
items.note: Self-contained combinatorial target. Equality does not follow from symmetry alone.

items.name: Counterexample to automatic equality
items.statement: The array a(0,1)=a(0,-1)=1, zero elsewhere, satisfies the symmetry relation but has row weights concentrated at 0 and column weights at -1 and 1.

items.name: Additional local hypothesis removes extraneous points
items.statement: Under Theorem 1.11, suppose pi_u=AZ(sigma) for an irreducible discrete-series sigma whose pure Weil-Deligne nilpotent operator belongs to the same orbit N as the chosen spherical place. The source concludes that every split unramified real Satake parameter is h_N/2.
items.note: Retain the chosen compatible global parameter and same-orbit hypothesis. Several printed weight comparisons in the proof have n_v on both sides and need independent checking. Resolved: the rightmost subscripts are n_u (sourceIssues E3); the F4 comparison also needs the corrected B3 coordinate (E5). The review recomputed (n_u, n_v) for the F4, E7 and E8 cases by root enumeration. Additional gate from E18: any use of Theorem8.5/Remark8.7 must either establish the real/central-compact hypothesis at every place of use or import a newly exhaustive arbitrary-compact classification with centralizer-of-s_c and orbit tracking. A geometric parameter with connected center alone is insufficient. Preserve the separate gap from real-part recognition to nilpotent-stratum recognition. The local G2 witness is not asserted to occur in a global cuspidal packet; no global counterexample is claimed.
items.proofState: Unproved target: existing global-parametrization/stratum obligations plus the explicit compact-part classification gate; not solved by this fix.

items.name: Theorem 3.8 (semisimple local parametrization), parts (2)–(3)
items.statement: There is a semisimple local parametrization L_F : Π(G/F) → Φ(G/F) (Genestier–Lafforgue; Fargues–Scholze) compatible with parabolic induction; in particular, if L_F(π) is irreducible, then π is supercuspidal.
items.note: ES5 plans the semisimple parameter assignment and ES7:parabolic its compatibility with parabolic induction (FS IX.7.3); (3) follows from (2). Part (1), local–global compatibility, is item semisimple-local-global.

items.name: Li-Huerta: Genestier–Lafforgue equals Fargues–Scholze
items.statement: For F a local field of positive characteristic, the semisimple local parametrizations of Genestier–Lafforgue and of Fargues–Scholze coincide ([LH], arXiv:2301.09711).
items.note: Cited input that makes Theorem 3.8 independent of the construction; routed to the Ramanujan–Arthur Part II.

items.name: Proposition 3.10(1): Galois conjugates of geometric representations
items.statement: If π is geometric, then for every embedding ι′ : E → Q̄_ℓ the representation π_E ⊗_{E,ι′} Q̄_ℓ is again geometric.
items.note: Compatibility of the Genestier–Lafforgue and Fargues–Scholze parametrizations with automorphisms of Q̄_ℓ.

items.name: Proposition 3.10(2): geometric characters of tori
items.statement: If G is a torus, π is geometric if and only if π takes values in the group of Weil q-numbers.
items.note: Reduce to G_m and local class field theory.

items.name: Proposition 3.10(3): stability of geometricity
items.statement: Geometricity is preserved under normalized parabolic induction, Jacquet modules, direct products, and twisting by geometric characters.

items.name: Proposition 3.10(4): central characters
items.statement: For any reductive G, if π is geometric then so is its central character.
items.note: Restriction to Z_G corresponds to the representations τ of LG factoring through the L-group of Z_G.

items.name: Arthur's conjectures in Clozel's simplified form (Conjectures 1.3, 1.8; Expectation 1.9)
items.statement: Conjecturally A_disc(G, U, C) = ⊕_{ψ ∈ Ψ(G,U)} A_{disc,U,ψ} with finite packets of unitary representations; for unramified w the Satake parameter s(π_w) has integral weights, equals ψ_w(Frob_w, j(Frob_w)), and ψ_w restricted to W_w/I_w is isobaric of weight 0; so the weights at unramified places depend only on the nilpotent class N_ψ.
items.note: Conjectural statements, recorded as the target the Part II's theorems (5.4, 1.11, 10.3) verify under hypotheses; they are not formalization targets as theorems.

items.name: Expectation 5.9 and the purity sketch 5.10 (alternative route)
items.statement: Expectation: the irreducible components of L(π, τ) occur in Rf_!(Q̄_ℓ) for a finite-type morphism of stacks f : Z → C ∖ |S′| (moduli of shtukas), for τ adjoint and τ = τ₀. Granting this, every component is punctually ι-pure with integer weights, since ι-mixedness is preserved by the six operations on Artin stacks (Sun, ANT 6 (2012), Thm. 2.11) and integrality of weights reduces to Deligne's theorem for schemes. Lafforgue–Zhu prove the expectation for elliptic parameters.
items.note: An alternative to the tempered-anchor proof of Theorem 5.4; the sketch (credited to Olsson) is not a complete proof.

items.name: Xue's extension of the excursion parametrization
items.statement: Lafforgue's decomposition (3.3) and Satake compatibility extend to quotients of the compactly supported functions A_c(G, U, Q̄_ℓ) by ideals of finite codimension in H^S(G, U) (Xue, Épijournal Géom. Algébrique 4 (2020)); so Conjectures 9.1 and 9.5 hold for the discrete representations arising in such quotients.
items.note: The source does not claim this for every residual representation; the parametrization hypothesis of Theorem 1.11 is stated accordingly.

items.name: Genericity and hermitian criteria for spherical representations
items.statement: L(s) is generic iff X(s) is irreducible (Barbasch–Moy); for dominant ν ∈ C0, X(ν) = L(ν) iff ⟨α∨, ν⟩ ≠ 1 for all positive coroots α∨ (for general ν: ⟨α∨, ν⟩ ≠ ±1) (Casselman; [BC1, §3.1]); L(ν) admits a nonzero invariant hermitian form iff w₀(ν) = −ν, automatic when w0 = −1, i.e. for types B, C, D_{2m}, G2, F4, E7, E8 (the paper lists B, C, G2, F4, E7, E8).
items.note: Cited inputs defining the generic unitary region.

items.name: Lemma 6.7 (the fundamental alcove is unitary)
items.statement: A₀ ∩ C_{0,h} ⊆ U^g_0, where A₀ = {ν ∈ C₀ : ⟨γ∨, ν⟩ < 1} is the fundamental alcove.
items.note: Complementary-series deformation from ν = 0 (Knapp–Stein) up to the first reducibility wall γ∨ = 1.

items.name: Lemma 6.8 (unbounded regions are not unitary)
items.statement: If ν ∈ C₀ has ⟨α∨_i, ν⟩ > 1 for some simple coroot α∨_i, then ν ∉ U^g_0.

items.name: Theorem 6.9 (shape of the generic unitary locus)
items.statement: For G quasi-simple split adjoint, U^g_0 is the intersection of the hermitian locus C_{0,h} with a union of 2^d alcoves in C₀ including A₀, where d = 0 for PGL(n), SO(2n+1); ⌊(n−1)/2⌋ for PSp(2n); n − 1 for PSO(4n) (n ≥ 2) and PSO(4n+2) (n ≥ 1); 1 for G2, F4, E6; 3 for E7; 4 for E8.
items.locator: arXiv:2311.15300v1, §6, Theorem 6.9, p. 18 ([Ba, Ci1, Ci2, BC1])
items.note: Cited classification; the printed 'hermitian locus C₀' means C_{0,h} (sourceIssues E8). The hyperplane arrangement α∨ = 1 cuts C₀ into ∏(d_i + h)/d_i open regions (105 for F4, 25080 for E8).

items.name: Reduction of half-integrality to ν_i ∈ {0, ½} (6.11)–(6.13)
items.statement: If ⟨α∨, ν⟩ ∈ ε + ½Z for all coroots with 0 ≤ ε < ½, then ε ∈ {0, ¼}, and ε = 0 when G is quasi-simple of rank ≥ 2 (use α∨₁ + α∨₂). Writing ν = Σ ν_i ω_i, half-integrality means ν_i ∈ ½Z_{≥0}, and by Lemma 6.8 a generic unitary half-integral ν has ν_i ∈ {0, ½}.

items.name: Lemma 10.9 for classical Lie algebras
items.statement: For ǧ = sl(N), so(N), sp(N), sl(2)-subalgebras are classified up to Ǧ#-conjugacy (Ǧ# = SL(N), SO(N) for N odd, O(N) for N even, Sp(N)) by the partition of N given by the ǎ-module C^N ([CM, Thms. 5.1.1, 5.1.6, Obs. 5.1.7]), hence by the grading of C^N. For so(2n) and very even partitions, the two SO(2n)-orbits are separated by the top h-weight of the half-spin module S⁺: ½(a₁ + ⋯ + a_n) versus ½(−a₁ + a₂ + ⋯ + a_n).
items.locator: arXiv:2311.15300v1, Appendix, proof of Lemma 10.9, p. 35
items.note: The top-weight comparison was rechecked: with even sign changes the maximum on (−a₁, a₂, …) is attained with no sign change, since a₁ ≤ a_j. Stated with graded pieces (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Adjoint gradings separate exceptional nilpotent orbits
items.statement: For ǧ of type G2, F4, E6, E7 or E8, two sl(2)-triples whose neutral elements give the same multiplicities dim gr_i(ǧ) of ad(h)-eigenvalues on the adjoint representation are conjugate. Equivalently, the 5, 16, 21, 45 and 70 nilpotent orbits have pairwise distinct adjoint gradings.
items.locator: arXiv:2311.15300v1, Appendix, proof of Lemma 10.9, p. 35
items.note: Certified 29 Sep 2026 by exact rational computation. By Bala–Carter, orbits correspond to Levi subalgebras l with a distinguished parabolic of [l, l], and distinguished means dim g₀ = dim g₂ for the 0/2 labelling. Enumerating all subsets of simple nodes gave exactly 5, 16, 21, 45, 70 orbits (distinct dominant h) and as many distinct adjoint gradings. The paper checks E8, F4 and G2 in Mathematica; its E6/E7 inference is repaired by the direct computation (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: Tables 2–4: adjoint gradings of the nilpotent orbits of E8, F4, G2
items.statement: For each nilpotent orbit (Bala–Carter label) of E8, F4 and G2, the list dim gr_i(ǧ), i = 0, …, i_max, of ad(h)-eigenspace dimensions on the adjoint representation, as printed in Tables 2–4.
items.note: Certified 29 Sep 2026: all 91 printed rows (70 for E8, 16 for F4, 5 for G2) equal the computed gradings for the orbit with the printed label. Every i_max is right, the rows are pairwise distinct, and each row sums (with negative weights) to 248, 52 and 14. The entries are graded dimensions, not cumulative filtration dimensions (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Weil–Deligne purity of discrete series ([GHS]) and of tempered representations
items.statement: Source-gated input from the pending GHS owner: under GHSv3 Theorem1.2 hypotheses (connected reductive G over a local function field, p>3 in this version), a discrete series has a unique essentially tempered Weil–Deligne refinement of its Genestier–Lafforgue semisimple parameter. For semisimple G, Ad∘L(π) is pure of weight0 under Corollary3.11, for every embedding by Remark3.12. The geometric-central-character variant and extension to tempered representations require the exact source scope and central normalization; do not identify intrinsic purity with weight0 of every algebraic test representation for arbitrary reductive G.
items.locator: arXiv:2311.15300v1, §4.2 after Proposition 4.5, p. 12; proof of Theorem 5.4, p. 14; Theorem 10.3
items.note: The anchor of Theorem 5.4 and the hypothesis of Theorem 10.3. Proved in [GHS]; PAPER-GAN-HARRIS-SAWIN-ETAL-24's items 16 and 21 state it, on a route not yet accepted, so the design should import it from there once that owner is settled. Coordinate this input with the explicit early arithmetic-prefix/GHS request, retaining the pending supplier and its source hypotheses. It is not supplied by the final Theorem5.4 application or the unproved general geometricity sketch E10. The historical all-test-representations weight0 formulation is preserved separately as sourceClaimBeforeArithmeticSupplierRepair. The supplier must provide the intrinsic/central normalization needed by CH Definition2.6; the fresh GHSv3 source explicitly proves weight0 for Ad in semisimple scope. No arbitrary reductive central twist is silently normalized to zero.
items.sourceClaimBeforeArithmeticSupplierRepai: For π_u in the discrete series of G(K_u), K_u a local function field, and every representation τ of ^L G, τ∘L^ss(π_u) (the Genestier–Lafforgue semisimple parameter) extends uniquely to a pure Weil–Deligne representation (L^ss(π_u), N_{π_u}) of weight 0 in the sense of Definition 2.6 ([GHS, Theorem 1.2]); more generally the same holds for tempered π_u.

items.name: Spherical tempered representations are generic
items.statement: A spherical tempered representation of an unramified quasi-split G(K_w) is generic ([Re93, Prop. 7.4]; for split adjoint G, s = s_0 is compact, the q-eigenspace of Ad(s) is 0, and π_w is the full spherical principal series).
items.note: The whole content of Corollary 5.7 beyond Theorem 5.4.

routes.title: Representations of semisimple Lie algebras, highest weight theory, and the Weyl formulas, Part II: nilpotent orbits and weight patterns
routes.reason: The Tau Ceti roadmap LieHighestWeight supplies representation and weight theory, and its sl2 layer is built; nothing in the atlas owns nilpotent orbits, Jacobson–Morozov, Kostant conjugacy or the recognition of triples from filtrations. A Part II extends a Tau Ceti roadmap without re-planning it. The area is representations, as for the accepted LieHighestWeight Part IIs, and PAPER-MAO-WAN-ZHANG-26 proposes the same id, parent and title, so the two coalesce.
routes.brief: Import tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/LieHighestWeight (Representations of semisimple Lie algebras, highest weight theory, and the Weyl formulas), especially its sl2 classification, complete reducibility and integer spectrum (built in Tau Ceti: TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Sl2) and its character theory, and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups (Reductive groups) for the adjoint action. Build only the missing nilpotent-orbit, zero-triple and representation-indexed filtration interfaces. Prove Jacobson-Morozov and Kostant comparison, tensor-compatible filtrations and conjugacy recognition. Separate very-even orthogonal orbits using half-spin representations. Give finite root/weight certificates for exceptional computations, and distinguish cumulative filtrations from graded multiplicities. The endpoints, not a second highest-weight theory, are: (Lemma 2.4/10.9) for two sl2-triples in a semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, equal dim Fil_i(V) for every finite-dimensional representation V and every i implies conjugacy under the adjoint group; and (Proposition 10.2) two geometric semisimple parameters with identical weight patterns in every algebraic representation have Weyl-conjugate real parts. The exceptional adjoint gradings (Tables 2–4) are certified by a Bala–Carter enumeration, and that also covers E6 and E7 directly; a formal proof may reuse that finite certificate.

routes.title: Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: unitary spherical representations
routes.reason: SR.0-4 already own the category, induction, temperedness and Satake. They do not contain the root-by-root unitary complementary-series classification extracted here.
routes.brief: Import SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (Smooth representations of local groups), SR.2 for induction and Jacquet functors, SR.3 for admissibility and temperedness, and SR.4 for the relative Satake dictionary. Import SmoothRepresentationsPartIIUnitaryDual (proposed from PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B, accepted) for unitary and unitarizable representations and weak containment; LieHighestWeightPartIINilpotentOrbits for nilpotent orbits, Jacobson–Morozov and the triple centralizers; and ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction ES5 and ES7:parabolic for semisimple local parameters and their compatibility with parabolic induction. Construct Aubert-Zelevinsky and Kazhdan-Lusztig parameter comparisons, generic unitary regions, half-integral tests, centralizer reductions and the exceptional E8 region. Prove the split and nonsplit local temperedness tests with the odd-unitary exclusion, for real Satake parameters: if L(s_ν) is generic and unitary and ν is half-integral for the adjoint and the fundamental representations of Proposition 6.31, then ν = 0 (Corollary 6.32(1)); likewise for the nonsplit groups other than the quasi-split PSU(2n + 1) with the representations of G∨ ⋊ ⟨τ⟩ (Corollary 7.5). As printed for arbitrary s = s_c s_ν these fail (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E11, a G2 counterexample); the case of non-central s_c needs the Barbasch–Moy reduction to the centralizer of s_c. State Theorem8.5-derived Sp/Spin/exceptional lists only in the real or central-compact sector, with E5’s corrected F4 point. The unrestricted exceptional endpoint is false by the fully geometric G2 zero-orbit witness (E18 linked to E11). Audit the Sp/Spin interfaces at the same scope boundary and keep the finite E8,4A1 real-region exclusion separate. A general compact-part classification is an explicit new exhaustive target: analyze Z_{G∨}(s_c), its root datum/Hecke parameters, geometric eigenvalues in every representation, nilpotent q-eigenspace, centralizer orbit lifting, and unitarity/branching. Do not patch exhaustiveness by appending one G2 point. Distinguish full geometric Frobenius arithmetic from the real half-lattice condition. Include the genericity and hermitian criteria, Lemmas 6.7–6.8, Theorem 6.9 as the cited classification input, and the ε = 0 reduction (6.11)–(6.13). Theorem4.2 (galois-discrete-series) is moved to the early arithmetic portion of the global PartII; this local route owns no number-field globalization theorem and imports no whole global consumer. Its classification gates are handed to the global application portion, independently of that arithmetic prefix.

routes.title: Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields, Part II: Ramanujan and Arthur weight constraints
routes.reason: GS.5-7 supply parameters and comparisons; the local-to-global weight restrictions and conditional nongeneric endpoints are additional mathematics, not a rebuild of shtukas.
routes.brief: Import FunctionFieldArithmetic (Global function fields, reciprocity and automorphic foundations), FA.6 for the existing cuspidal coefficient and finiteness theory. Import GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands (Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields), GS.5 for cusp parameters, GS.6 for GLn purity and GS.7 for semisimple local-global compatibility. Import DeligneWeightsAndPurity (Deligne weights, purity and the Weil bounds), DWP.0, DWP.5 and DWP.8, SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (Smooth representations of local groups), SR.2-4, and ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction ES5 and ES7:parabolic for the semisimple local parameters that Li-Huerta compares with Genestier–Lafforgue. Use the proposed nilpotent-weight and unitary-spherical extensions as suppliers to the later application portion only. First build an explicitly early arithmetic prefix containing galois-discrete-series, geometric-discrete-series, ghs-discrete-series-purity and the required embedding-independence interface, using FA.6,GS.5/GS.7,SR.2/SR.3 and DWP.0/5/8. Its GHS globalization/purity input is source-gated and coordinated with the pending SupercuspidalParameters owner (currently held for revision), with semisimple group and finite/geometric central-character scope, precise local isolation/support-descent and residue-characteristic hypotheses. Never derive that input from Theorem5.4 or the general sketch step covered by E10. Then build the local geometricity anchor, constant-field twist removal, finite-extension parameter lifting and weight-pattern propagation, and target Theorem5.4: for K a global function field, G connected absolutely simple over K and π cuspidal, if π_v is generic at an unramified quasi-split place v (G(K_v) not the quasi-split odd unitary form) and π_u is discrete series (more generally tempered) at some place u, then π_w is tempered at every place w where π is unramified and G is unramified quasi-split. The v1 proof has three holes to fill: Corollary 6.32(1) for non-central compact parts (E11), the sketch of Theorem 4.3 (E10), and the reduction to adjoint G for types A, B and E7 (E12). Then Theorem 1.11 (under Conjectures 9.1 and 9.5, or a parametrization as in [Laf18]: with a split place v where π_v is in the complementary series of the nilpotent class of N and a geometric place u ∈ S, every split unramified π_w is in the same complementary series, with real part the central point or an extraneous point of Theorem 8.5) and Theorem 10.3 (if moreover π_u = AZ(σ) for a discrete series σ with Weil–Deligne parameter (ϕ_σ, N), the real parts are the central point, so no extraneous point occurs). State the discrete-spectrum conclusions only with the actual parametrization hypotheses; construct the finite-array comparison and explicit exclusion tests before Theorem 10.3. Do not assume arbitrary automorphic base change or the Arthur conjectures. Include Proposition 3.10(1)–(4), Li-Huerta's comparison, Xue's extension to finite-codimension Hecke quotients, and the stack-purity alternative (Expectation 5.9, Sketch 5.10). Record Arthur's conjectures only as the conjectural target. Every downstream use of Theorem8.5/Remark8.7 has an explicit gate: prove the real/central-compact hypothesis at that place or supply a newly exhaustive arbitrary-compact classification. E18 rejects the ungated exceptional list even with full geometricity and connected center. Keep the existing real-part-to-nilpotent-stratum gap open; no global counterexample or completion of its proof is inferred from the local witness. The design order is base arithmetic plus the gated GHS obligation → arithmetic prefix; local unitary classification and nilpotent recognition proceed separately; those prefixes → global applications. No whole consumer feeds its prerequisite.
